issues.legal_issue: Whether the agreements to sell were validly executed and proved.
Whether execution of a registered power of attorney by the seller created suspicion about the transaction.
Whether the purchasers’ failure to testify personally required an adverse inference when witnesses with personal knowledge testified on their behalf.
Whether the suits for specific performance were barred by limitation.
Whether the defendants proved their allegations that the agreements to sell were forged or fraudulent.
Whether the failure of a principal heir to testify affected the defendants’ case.
Whether the seller qualified as a pardanashin woman entitled to special protection in relation to the documents.
Whether the purchasers’ possession of the original title deed and revenue record supported the validity of the transaction.
Whether the purchasers had possession of the property under the agreements to sell.
Whether transfers made in violation of an interim injunction affected the validity of the transfers and the conduct of the transferring parties.
Whether readiness and willingness to perform was required where the purchasers had paid the entire consideration.
Whether the property was sufficiently identified in the agreements despite the absence of express boundary details.
Whether transfers made during the pending litigation could prejudice the purchasers’ rights under the prior agreements to sell.
